knowledge:
- key_parameters: file=Prefix for intermediate output files generated during analysis (e.g., nhits, scores, permutations) ;; chr=Vector of chromosome names to analyze ;; chrL=Vector of chromosome lengths corresponding to the chr parameter ;; times=Scaling factor/multiplier used in ChIPseqScore and score2wig to control precision ;; nn=Permutation run identifier/index used in permutatedWinScores and getPermutatedWinScores ;; FDR=False discovery rate threshold (e.g., 0.05) used to calculate the score threshold
- alternatives: multtest=Mentioned as an alternative R package for multiple testing correction that could be less conservative than the built-in FDR calculation
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing ChIP-seq data to identify protein-bound genomic regions (peaks) at single-nucleotide resolution, especially when a control sample is available and permutation-based FDR control is desired
- pitfalls: PCR artifacts can cause high numbers of duplicated reads. CSAR requires that the number of extended reads overlapping a position is supported by both strands independently (taking the minimum value of both strands). If strand information is missing, incorrect, or poorly balanced, this strand-independent validation step may fail or lead to loss of signal

workflows.name: chip_seq_peak_calling_and_annotation
workflows.intent: Identify protein-bound genomic regions from ChIP-seq data, map them to genes, and calculate FDR thresholds using permutation.
input: sample_reads.tsv (mapped ChIP-seq sample reads with columns Nhits, lengthRead, strand, chr, pos)
control_reads.tsv (mapped ChIP-seq control reads with columns Nhits, lengthRead, strand, chr, pos)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate extended read overlaps per nucleotide using mappedReads2Nhits ;; 2. Calculate read-enrichment scores using ChIPseqScore ;; 3. Identify candidate enriched regions using sigWin ;; 4. Export scores to WIG format using score2wig ;; 5. Calculate distance of candidate regions to genes using distance2Genes ;; 6. Identify genes with peaks using genesWithPeaks ;; 7. Generate permutated datasets and calculate permutated window scores using permutatedWinScores ;; 8. Load permutated scores using getPermutatedWinScores ;; 9. Calculate FDR threshold using getThreshold
workflows.code:
library(CSAR)
data("CSAR-dataset");
head(sampleSEP3_test)
head(controlSEP3_test)
nhitsS<-mappedReads2Nhits(sampleSEP3_test,file="sampleSEP3_test",chr=c("CHR1v01212004"),chrL=c(10000))
nhitsC<-mappedReads2Nhits(controlSEP3_test,file="controlSEP3_test",chr=c("CHR1v01212004"),chrL=c(10000))
nhitsC$filenames
nhitsS$filenames
test<-ChIPseqScore(control=nhitsC,sample=nhitsS,file="test",times=10000)
test$filenames
win<-sigWin(test)
head(win)
score2wig(test,file="test.wig",times=10000)
d<-distance2Genes(win=win,gff=TAIR8_genes_test)
d
genes<-genesWithPeaks(d)
head(genes)
permutatedWinScores(nn=1,sample=sampleSEP3_test,control=controlSEP3_test,fileOutput="test",chr=c("CHR1v01212004"),chrL=c(100000))
permutatedWinScores(nn=2,sample=sampleSEP3_test,control=controlSEP3_test,fileOutput="test",chr=c("CHR1v01212004"),chrL=c(100000))
nulldist<-getPermutatedWinScores(file="test",nn=1:2)
getThreshold(winscores=values(win)$score,permutatedScores=nulldist,FDR=.05)
